title: Methods of protest and change

draft.title: Methods of protest and change
card: Movements for change choose methods to pressure those in power. Common methods are non-violent protest, legal action, using the media, and sometimes violence.
Non-violent protest
marches, boycotts, strikes and sit-ins. They show how many people support a cause and can disrupt business as usual.
Legal action
taking a case to court or pushing for new laws. It can change rules, but it is often slow.
Media

newspapers, photographs and television can spread a cause to people far away and win public sympathy. Violence has been used by some movements, and it can lose public support or lead to harsher crackdowns.
draft.remember: Each method has strengths and risks, and movements often combined several.

a.q: Why did movements often use the media as part of their campaigns?
opts: To spread their cause and win wider public sympathy
To avoid the need for any other method of protest
To force courts to change the law straight away
To stop the government from responding to them
a.why: Newspapers, photographs and television carried a cause to people who had never seen it first-hand. This could build sympathy. The media did not replace other methods or force the courts to act.
a.clue: Think about who could see a photograph in a newspaper.

b.q: In 1955 in the city of Marlow, a group of workers refused to ride the buses for a year to protest unfair seating rules. At the same time, their lawyers took the bus company to court. Which description fits their approach?
opts: A boycott combined with legal action
Legal action alone, since the boycott was passive
A violent campaign backed by a court case
Media coverage only, with no direct pressure
b.why: Refusing to ride the buses is a non-violent boycott, and the court case is legal action. Using both at once is a combination of methods. It is wrong to call the boycott legal action alone, because it was a protest that cost the company money.
b.clue: Count how many separate methods the group used.

a.best: To spread their cause and win wider public sympathy

b.best: A boycott combined with legal action

problems.detail: The sentence on violence sits inside the Media bullet. A student could read violence as a kind of media method. It should be its own bullet.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and both explanations match the card. The only problem is that the sentence on violence is placed inside the Media bullet, which could confuse students.
